title: Bharata through the ages
body: A few centuries after the Mahabharata, 'Bharata' became the name generally used for the Indian Subcontinent. An ancient text, the Vishnu Purana, says: 'The country that lies north of the ocean and south of the snowy mountains is called Bharata.' Far in the south, a poem of ancient Tamil literature from about 2,000 years ago praises a king whose name is known 'from Kumari in the south, from the great mountain in the north, from the oceans on the east and on the west'. Centuries later, the Constitution of India, which came into force in 1950 and was first written in English, uses the phrase 'India, that is Bharat' right at the beginning, and its Hindi version says 'Bharat arthat India'. Today the name is generally written 'Bharat' in north India and often 'Bharatam' in south India.
